=== NEW 3. THE `head.startswith(reviewed)` DEFECT IS WIDER THAN "NAMES NO COMMIT", AND I CAN SAY WHY ===
Reviewers before me found that scripts/lwb_auto_queue.py:206 counts a review record with no
reviewed_commit, because head.startswith("") is True. Confirmed, and generalised. I monkeypatched
_list_dir/_contents_json and called review_records(29, "727751fa...") directly:
    1 accepted | reviewed_commit field ABSENT         | problems=[]
    1 accepted | reviewed_commit ""                   | problems=[]
    1 accepted | reviewed_commit "7"  (ONE CHARACTER) | problems=[]
    0 accepted | reviewed_commit ae29b1a9... (real, older sha) | rejected, "is not this head"
So it is not only the empty case: ANY prefix of the head passes, down to a single character, and
1 of 16 single hex characters matches any given head by chance. The check is non-vacuous only
against a sha that is genuinely wrong.
THE ROOT CAUSE, which is the part I think is worth fixing rather than patching: the prefix
comparison is borrowed from scripts/lwb_lanes.py, where it is SAFE — because lanes loads
reviews/schema.json and enforces its `"pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$"` on reviewed_commit first, so a
prefix shorter than 7 hex characters cannot reach the comparison. lwb_auto_queue.py reuses the
comparison without the validation that makes it sound: it reads the fields straight off the parsed
JSON and never validates the record shape at all. Fixing line 206 alone leaves the same class of
hole in every other field it reads. The schema check is the missing piece.

=== RE-MEASURED AT THIS HEAD, NOT INHERITED — the known blockers all still stand ===
- The PR does not merge: REST pulls/29 -> mergeable_state dirty; merge-tree against live main
  conflicts. No pull_request CI can run, which is why NEW 2 looks the way it does.
- The suite is RED here: python -m pytest tests/ -q -> 1 failed, 514 passed.
  tests/test_lwb_check_env_leak.py::test_success_path_prints_no_needle_count fails, and its
  assertion message is the real finding: lwb_check_env_leak.py flags
  reviews/29/cloud-reviewer-b.json:10 and reviews/29/cloud-reviewer.json:10 for "absolute path to
  a python interpreter".
  I VERIFIED THIS IS A FALSE POSITIVE, independently of the reviewer who first reported it, by
  probing the regex directly rather than trusting either of us. HARDCODED_INTERPRETER is
    (?:[A-Za-z]:\\|/)(?:[\w.\-]+[\\/])*python3?(?:\.exe)?(?=[\s\"'`]|$)
  Its leading alternative is a bare slash and its path-segment group may match ZERO times, so
  ordinary English prose in which a word is joined by a forward slash to the word python matches
  it. Fed that prose it returns True; fed two genuine interpreter paths it also returns True; fed
  unrelated text, False. So the check is not vacuous — it is over-broad, and it is firing on
  reviewer prose, not on a leak. The file is pre-existing on main and is NOT changed by this PR, so
  this is not this PR's defect; it is nonetheless red on this PR's head and on nothing else's,
  because this is where the prose lives. That is the failure mode that gets a gate switched off,
  and it is worth an owner's attention on its own.
- lwb-check-state-claims is RED: HANDOFF.md:37 names main f9b4dea, live main is bfe8507. NEAR-MISS
  I AM RECORDING: this is exactly the accusation a stale clone makes falsely, and my brief warns

  stand. It stands, and it is main drifting under a correctly generated block, not a hand-asserted

=== A SECOND NEAR-MISS OF MY OWN, PRINTED RATHER THAN HIDDEN ===
Earlier in this same run I measured gate exit codes as `cmd | tail -n; echo $?`, which reports
TAIL's status, not the script's. Every gate read as passing, including ones that had failed. I
caught it when a script printed an argparse usage error and still reported success. Every exit code
in this record was re-measured without a pipe. Had I not caught it I would have certified red gates
as green — on this PR, that would have meant missing the failing test, the state-claims failure and
both identity failures at once.
